data.hypothesis: In the O(N²) pair loop, factoring out the target mass removes repeated target-mass arithmetic, while explicit rsqrtf-based inverse-distance cubing replaces sqrtf, denominator multiplication, and per-pair division. This may reduce instruction cost without shared-memory tiling or target coarsening; the approximate reciprocal square root and altered accumulation require correctness and tolerance validation.
data.notes: Only src/nbody_kernel.cu is changed; the launch configuration and one-output-per-thread structure are unchanged. The baseline is valid at mean_seconds 0.0018473421 (baseline-e1); no candidate timing or speedup is known. The controller should validate edge cases and the independent oracle, then compare the official geometric-mean objective. Consulted the NVIDIA CUDA Best Practices Guide snapshot (13.4 publisher-current); the target/compiler version was not supplied, so no target-specific performance claim is made.
transformations: Cache the output particle in a local variable and use its coordinates throughout the pair loop.
Accumulate acceleration with source mass after algebraically cancelling the target mass from force divided by target mass.
Use rsqrtf(distSq) and explicit multiplication to form inverse distance cubed, avoiding sqrtf and per-pair division.
Apply a target-mass identity factor once after the acceleration reduction to retain non-finite behavior for zero or non-finite target masses.
